Celebrity fan-out, global merge, prefix search and politeness.

These **4 independent interview problems** are intended to train deep reasoning, not an oversized implementation.

1. [**The Celebrity Fan-Out Problem**](../04-social-search-and-crawling/celebrity-news-feed.qmd) — Normal users have 200 followers; a celebrity has 30 million.

2. [**Exact Global Top-K from Distributed Search Shards**](../04-social-search-and-crawling/distributed-topk-search.qmd) — Each shard sends candidates; can the coordinator produce the true top ten?

3. [**Search Autocomplete Under a Strict Latency Budget**](../04-social-search-and-crawling/autocomplete-index.qmd) — Predict the next word with bounded prefix work, ranking and updating.

4. [**A Web Crawler That Does Not Overload One Host**](../04-social-search-and-crawling/polite-web-crawler.qmd) — Distribute crawling while observing host-specific delays, deduplication and safe fetching.

## The learning contract

For each problem identify the naive solution, exhibit a failure, derive the invariant, prove the correction, then reproduce a small part with the [NestJS lab](../lab/README.md). Production distribution requires extra atomicity, shared state or durable messaging where indicated.

$$
\text{Design}=\text{State}\ +\ \text{Transitions}\ +\ \text{Invariants}\ +\ \text{Failure model}.
$$

This is a **conceptual decomposition**, not a numeric equation.
